title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Malfunction
shortDescription: EGR system is not flowing exhaust gas as commanded.
fullDescription: The PCM has determined that the EGR system is not flowing exhaust into the intake at the commanded rate. This is detected by the lack of expected change in MAP, MAF, or oxygen-sensor readings when EGR is commanded open.
safetyImpact: Emissions and EGR faults rarely create immediate safety risks but can lead to drivability issues and catalyst damage if ignored.

causes.cause: Carbon buildup on EGR valve, throttle body, or intake runners
Failed EGR valve, position sensor, or solenoid
Damaged or aged catalyst substrate / loss of ceramic coating
Wiring or connector corrosion at the affected sensor or actuator
Vacuum or exhaust leak misleading the OBD monitor
Loose or damaged fuel filler cap (EVAP-related faults)

symptoms: Rough idle, hesitation, or pinging on acceleration

fixSteps.title: Verify code with scan tool
fixSteps.instruction: Read all stored and pending codes, then look at relevant PIDs (commanded EGR vs. actual, downstream O2 voltage, EVAP purge duty cycle, fuel tank pressure).

fixSteps.title: Inspect for vacuum and exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Use a smoke machine to find vacuum or EVAP leaks. Inspect the exhaust ahead of the affected oxygen sensor for cracks, loose flanges, or rusted gaskets.

fixSteps.title: Test the affected actuator/sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Following the wiring diagram, back-probe the connector and verify reference voltage, ground, and signal. Replace components that fall outside spec.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the EGR valve, secondary air switching valve, or affected sensor and clean carbon buildup or replace as needed. For catalyst codes, replace the converter only after upstream issues are resolved.

faq.q: Will this code make me fail emissions testing?
faq.a: Yes. Any active emissions-related DTC, plus an unfinished readiness monitor, will cause an automatic failure in OBD-based smog programs.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive?
faq.a: Drivability is usually only mildly affected, but ignoring the fault can lead to catalyst damage, which is far more expensive to repair than the original problem.

faq.q: Could a loose gas cap really set this code?
faq.a: On EVAP faults like P0440 / P0455, a loose or worn fuel cap is one of the most common single causes — always tighten and recheck before deeper diagnostics.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive?
faq.a: Drivability is usually only mildly affected, but ignoring the fault can lead to catalyst damage, which is far more expensive to repair than the original problem.

faq.q: Could a loose gas cap really set this code?
faq.a: On EVAP faults like P0440 / P0455, a loose or worn fuel cap is one of the most common single causes — always tighten and recheck before deeper diagnostics.

title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Bank 2
shortDescription: Electrical fault on the bank 2 catalyst heater circuit.
fullDescription: An open or short has been detected on the bank 2 catalyst heater control circuit, preventing the catalyst from reaching light-off temperature quickly.
safetyImpact: Emissions and EGR faults rarely create immediate safety risks but can lead to drivability issues and catalyst damage if ignored.

causes.cause: Carbon buildup on EGR valve, throttle body, or intake runners
Failed EGR valve, position sensor, or solenoid
Damaged or aged catalyst substrate / loss of ceramic coating
Wiring or connector corrosion at the affected sensor or actuator
Vacuum or exhaust leak misleading the OBD monitor
Loose or damaged fuel filler cap (EVAP-related faults)

symptoms: Rough idle, hesitation, or pinging on acceleration

fixSteps.title: Verify code with scan tool
fixSteps.instruction: Read all stored and pending codes, then look at relevant PIDs (commanded EGR vs. actual, downstream O2 voltage, EVAP purge duty cycle, fuel tank pressure).

fixSteps.title: Inspect for vacuum and exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Use a smoke machine to find vacuum or EVAP leaks. Inspect the exhaust ahead of the affected oxygen sensor for cracks, loose flanges, or rusted gaskets.

fixSteps.title: Test the affected actuator/sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Following the wiring diagram, back-probe the connector and verify reference voltage, ground, and signal. Replace components that fall outside spec.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the EGR valve, secondary air switching valve, or affected sensor and clean carbon buildup or replace as needed. For catalyst codes, replace the converter only after upstream issues are resolved.
